title: Short Vowels in CVC Closed Syllables (/æ/, /ɛ/, /ɪ/, /ɒ/, /ʌ/)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: Short Vowels in CVC Closed Syllables (/æ/, /ɛ/, /ɪ/, /ɒ/, /ʌ/). Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner pronounces 'cut' and 'cat' identically.
💡 Solution: Use mouth opening mirror: /æ/ requires wide jaw drop; /ʌ/ is neutral central.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Short Vowels in CVC Closed Syllables (/æ/, /ɛ/, /ɪ/, /ɒ/, /ʌ/)
1. Definition: A closed syllable ends in a consonant and locks the vowel into its short sound.
2. Rule: Single vowel + ending consonant(s) = short vowel (/æ/ cat, /ɛ/ bed, /ɪ/ sit, /ɒ/ hot, /ʌ/ cup).
3. Why? The following consonant prevents the vowel from opening into its long name sound.
4. How to recognize? Look for CVC or VC word patterns.
5. Common examples: cat /kæt/, bed /bɛd/, sit /sɪt/, hot /hɒt/, cup /kʌp/, map, red, big, dog, bus
6. Counter-examples: he, she, go (open syllables ending in vowel = long sound).
7. Exceptions: Words with silent e (cake, home) or r-controlled vowels (car, for).
8. Common mistakes: Confusing short /æ/ (cat) with short /ʌ/ (cut) or short /ɛ/ (pet) with /ɪ/ (pit).
9. Mnemonic / Hint: CVC = Short Vowel! The consonant closes the door on the vowel!
10. Key vocabulary: closed syllable, short vowel, CVC, contrast, jaw drop
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟢 A1
13. Associated Visual: 🚪 Consonant door closing on the short vowel.
14. Key Takeaway: CVC pattern = Short Vowel sound always!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Does a closed syllable end in a vowel or a consonant? (Consonant)
CCQ 2: What is the vowel sound in 'cat'? (Short /æ/)
CCQ 3: How does 'sit' differ from 'site'? ('sit' is CVC short vowel; 'site' has Magic E)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Pronounce these CVC minimal pairs carefully:
🎯 Item: cat /kæt/ vs cut /kʌt/ ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /æ/ vs /ʌ/
🎯 Item: sit /sɪt/ vs set /sɛt/ ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /ɪ/ vs /ɛ/
